'''Isaiah T. Stevens''' (born November 1, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Stockton Kings]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State Rams]].

==High school career==
Stevens attended [[Allen High School (Texas)|Allen High School]] in [[Allen, Texas]]. As a junior, he led his team to the Class 6A state title.<ref>{{cite web|first=Kevin|last=Lytle|title=CSU basketball signee Isaiah Stevens has game the size of Texas|url=https://www.coloradoan.com/story/sports/csu/mens-basketball/2019/01/18/isaiah-stevens-basketball-recruiting-colorado-state-basketball/2589541002/|work=[[Fort Collins Coloradoan]]|date=January 18, 2019|access-date=February 4, 2021}}</ref> In his senior season, Stevens averaged 21 points and was named District 9-6A co-MVP.<ref>{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Welch|title=Boys Basketball: Allen's Stevens, Jesuit's Abmas split MVP nod in 9-6A all-district team|url=https://starlocalmedia.com/allenamerican/sports/boys-basketball-allens-stevens-jesuits-abmas-split-mvp-nod-in-9-6a-all-district-team/article_1fbe8986-3cfe-11e9-a8a2-8bbc1e20d47c.html|work=[[Allen American]]|date=March 2, 2019|access-date=February 4, 2021}}</ref> He competed for Team Faith on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit alongside five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] [[Greg Brown III]]. Stevens committed to playing college basketball for [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]] over offers from [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]] and [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]], among others.<ref>{{cite web|first=Eddie|last=Herz|title=CSU begins their 2019 recruiting class off with a guard|url=https://collegian.com/2018/08/csu-begins-their-2019-recruiting-class-off-with-a-guard/|work=[[Rocky Mountain Collegian]]|date=August 27, 2018|access-date=February 4, 2021|archive-date=October 11, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191011021343/https://collegian.com/2018/08/csu-begins-their-2019-recruiting-class-off-with-a-guard/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==
Stevens began his collegiate career as the starting point guard for the [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State Rams]], a role he would maintain throughout his decorated career. On December 22, 2019, Stevens recorded a freshman season-high 26 points, 12 assists and five steals in a 111–104 win over [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa]] in triple overtime.<ref>{{cite web|first=Eddie|last=Herz|title=Colorado State point guard Isaiah Stevens has never feared the moment|url=https://www.reporterherald.com/2019/12/27/colorado-state-point-guard-isaiah-stevens-has-never-feared-the-moment/|work=[[Reporter-Herald]]|date=December 27, 2019|access-date=February 4, 2021}}</ref> On January 29, 2020, he made a game-winning [[buzzer beater]] as part of a 12-point effort in a 92–91 victory over [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Eddie|last=Herz|title=Moby Madness: Isaiah Stevens delivers at the buzzer as CSU knocks off Nevada|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2020/01/29/isaiah-stevens-stevens-buries-winner-as-colorado-state-tops-nevada/|work=[[The Denver Post]]|date=January 29, 2020|access-date=February 4, 2021}}</ref> As a freshman, Stevens averaged 13.3 points, 4.5 assists and 3.1 rebounds per game, setting the program freshman record for assists. He earned [[Mountain West Conference|Mountain West]] Freshman of the Year honors and was selected to the Third Team All-Mountain West by the league's coaches.<ref>{{cite web|first=Kevin|last=Lytle|title=Colorado State basketball guard Isaiah Stevens named Mountain West Freshman of the Year|url=https://www.coloradoan.com/story/sports/csu/mens-basketball/2020/03/02/colorado-state-basketball-isaiah-stevens-mountain-west-freshman-year/4928215002/|work=[[Fort Collins Coloradoan]]|date=March 2, 2020|access-date=February 4, 2021}}</ref>

As a sophomore, Stevens averaged 15.3 points, 5.4 assists and 4.3 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite news|first=Brian|last=Bennett|title=St. Bonaventure, Colorado State, Loyola Chicago headline early mid-major top 10|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2644748/2021/06/16/st-bonaventure-colorado-state-loyola-chicago-headline-early-mid-major-top-10/|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=June 16, 2021|access-date=September 6, 2021}}</ref> He was named to the Second Team All-Mountain West.<ref>{{cite web|title=Medved Named MW Coach of the Year By League's Media, Roddy First Team and Stevens Second Team|url=https://csurams.com/news/2021/3/8/mens-basketball-medved-named-mw-coach-of-the-year-by-leagues-media-roddy-first-team-and-stevens-second-team.aspx|work=[[Colorado State Rams]]|date=March 8, 2021|access-date=September 5, 2021}}</ref> The Rams finished the [[2020-21 Colorado State Rams men's basketball team|2020-21 season]] with a 20-8 record while making it to the semifinals of the [[2021 National Invitation Tournament|NIT tournament]] before falling to [[2020-21 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team|Memphis]].

As a junior, Stevens averaged 14.7 points, 4.7 assists, and 3.2 rebounds per game. On January 28, 2022, Stevens scored a career high 35 points against [[2021–22 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team|UNLV]].<ref>https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401364757</ref> Stevens was named to the Second Team All-Mountain West.<ref name=MWCAwards>{{cite press release|title=Mountain West Reveals 2021-22 Men's Basketball All-Conference Teams|url=https://themw.com/news/2022/3/8/athlete-awards-mountain-west-reveals-2021-22-mens-basketball-all-conference-teams.aspx|website=TheMW.com|publisher=[[Mountain West Conference]]|date=March 8, 2022|access-date=March 8, 2022}}</ref> Stevens helped lead the Rams to their first [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Tournament]] appearance since 2013, securing a No. 6 seed—the highest in program history. The Rams finished the season ranked in the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball rankings|top 25 AP poll]] for the first time in school history.<ref>https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10029703-ap-college-basketball-poll-2022-final-rankings-released-before-march-madness</ref>

As a senior, Stevens averaged 17.9 points, 6.7 assists, and 3.4 rebounds per game. Stevens lead the conference in assists per game and was named to the First Team All-Mountain West.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-07 |title=Mountain West Reveals 2022-23 Men’s Basketball All-Conference Teams |url=https://themw.com/news/2023/03/07/athlete-awards-mountain-west-reveals-2022-23-mens-basketball-all-conference-teams-2/ |access-date=2025-07-10 |website=Mountain West Conference |language=en-US}}</ref>

In his final collegiate season, Stevens was named Mountain West preseason player of the year.<ref>https://www.denverpost.com/2023/10/12/csus-isaiah-stevens-named-mountain-west-preseason-player-of-the-year/</ref> On November 11, 2023, Stevens set a Colorado State single-game record by recording 14 assists.<ref>https://www.coloradoan.com/story/sports/csu/mens-basketball/2023/11/10/colorado-state-basketball-blows-out-wright-state/71530127007/</ref> On January 2, 2024, Stevens surpassed 2,000 career points.<ref>{{cite web|title=No. 13 Colorado State stops UNM in MW opener|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/basketball/no-13-colorado-state-stops-unm-mw-opener-2024-01-03/|website=Reuters.com|publisher=[[Reuters]]|date=January 3, 2024|access-date=January 3, 2024|quote=Fifth-year senior Isaiah Stevens finished with 18 points and eight assists for the Rams, giving him 2,017 career points.}}</ref> Stevens led [[2023–24 Colorado State Rams men's basketball team|Colorado State]] to its highest AP Poll ranking in program history, reaching No. 13.<ref>https://csurams.com/news/2023/12/4/mens-basketball-no-12-13-rams-make-program-history</ref> The Rams would appear in the Top 25 nine times throughout that season, a school record. The Rams would also return to the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Tournament]], earning a 67–42 win over [[2023–24 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] in the First Four before falling to [[2023–24 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas]] in the Round of 64. Stevens averaged 16.0 points, 6.8 assists, and 3.2 rebounds per game. He set a single season school record with 245 assists and once again lead the conference in assists per game. <ref>https://themw.com/news/2024/06/28/stevens-signs-with-miami-heat/</ref> He was named to the First Team All-Mountain West.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-03-12 |title=Mountain West Reveals 2023-24 Men’s Basketball All-Conference Teams |url=https://themw.com/news/2024/03/12/mountain-west-reveals-2023-24-mens-basketball-all-conference-teams/ |access-date=2025-07-10 |website=Mountain West Conference |language=en-US}}</ref>

Stevens is Colorado State's all-time leader in scoring (2,350), assists (863), and steals (158) among many other records.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Stevens Signs with Miami Heat |url=https://csurams.com/news/2024/6/27/mens-basketball-stevens-signs-with-miami-heat |access-date=2025-07-10 |website=Colorado State Athletics |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Stevens signed the [[Miami Heat]] to an Exhibit 10 contract on July 6, 2024,<ref>{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN ISAIAH STEVENS|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-isaiah-stevens|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 14, 2024}}</ref> but was waived on October 19.<ref>{{cite web|title=HEAT WAIVE LITTLE, PULLIN, STEVENS AND WASHINGTON|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-waive-little-pullin-stevens-and-washington|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 21, 2024}}</ref> On October 28, he joined the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Skyforce Announces Training Camp Roster Ahead of 2024-25 Season|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-training-camp-roster-ahead-of-2024-25-season|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=October 31, 2024}}</ref> and on December 26, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Heat.<ref>{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN ISAIAH STEVENS TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-isaiah-stevens-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 26, 2024|access-date=December 26, 2024}}</ref>

On July 7, 2025, Stevens signed a two-way contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Lytle | first=Kevin | title=Isaiah Stevens joins Nique Clifford on Sacramento Kings summer league | website=The Coloradoan | date=2025-07-07 | url=https://www.coloradoan.com/story/sports/csu/mens-basketball/2025/07/07/isaiah-stevens-joins-nique-clifford-on-sacramento-kings-summer-league/84490527007/ | access-date=2025-12-06}}</ref> Stevens appeared in three games for Sacramento, recording averages of 3.3 points, 1.0 rebounds, 3.3 assists, and 1.7 steals. On July 27, 2026, Stevens was waived by the Kings.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Isaiah Stevens: Let go by Sacramento|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/isaiah-stevens-let-go-by-sacramento/|access-date=August 27, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
